title: Whole-Slide Image Analysis under Realistic Few-Shot Annotation Protocols
abstract: arXiv:2608.30420v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automating the analysis of whole-slide images has high clinical value, since characterizing cancers requires examining them in detail. Such analysis increasingly relies on vision-language models that provide patch-level zero-shot predictions. However, these predictions remain noisy and must be refined with a few annotations. A promising paradigm for this refinement is few-shot transduction. Rather than treating each patch independently, these methods leverage the relations between patches, together with a few annotations, to refine all predictions jointly. translated_title: 现实少样本标注协议下的全切片图像分析
translated_abstract: 自动化全切片图像分析具有很高的临床价值，因为对癌症的表征需要对其进行详细检查。此类分析越来越依赖于能够提供图像块级零样本预测的视觉-语言模型。然而，这些预测仍然带有噪声，必须通过少量标注加以精炼。实现这种精炼的一个有前景的范式是少样本直推式学习。这类方法并非独立处理每个图像块，而是利用图像块之间的关系，结合少量标注，对所有预测进行联合精炼。然而，当前的直推式方法是在忽视了全切片图像关键特性的条件下进行评估的：(i) 数据集由从多张切片中提取的独立图像块组成，忽略了复杂的组织结构；(ii) 数据集大多是类别平衡的，而单个全切片图像则表现出严重的类别不平衡，某些类别甚至完全缺失；(iii) 标注……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文指出现有少样本直推式方法在评估全切片图像分析时忽视了组织结构、类别不平衡和标注协议等真实场景的关键特性，并提出了更贴近临床现实的少样本标注评估协议。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals that current few-shot transductive methods for whole-slide image analysis are evaluated under unrealistic conditions—ignoring tissue organization, severe class imbalance, and annotation constraints—and proposes realistic few-shot annotation protocols for more faithful evaluation.
